answer: Before each passage the tunnel keeper lights the lamps along the tunnel wall, and the record holds the lamp, the hour and the boat for every transit. A ember passage claimed as made fails the record: the lamps must have burned at the knoll of the tunnel, and a passage never made has no lamp to light. Forging a year of passages means hiring a keeper, faking sixty lamp entries and paying 8,900, while the echo record is compared with the boats' own logs, so a transit whose lamps were never lit never entered the dark.
